title: DSU / Union-Find & MST (Depth Pass)
relevance: High (second ladder after template Kruskal/Prim/component-size — CF Div2 C–E “rewrite as merges,” weighted DSU, Kruskal contribution, and MST variants that still show up as hard OA twists)
company_notes: Constraint satisfaction on equals/distances: assign values with given differences or check equation consistency — weighted DSU (People on a Line / Third Letter), same family as equality-equation DSU. Redeploy/recolor inside groups: friendship/swap/day-link components; minimize changes — Socks / New Year Permutation / K-Complete Word. Wire a network with a twist: connect all servers; fixed degree on one node / cheap hub / only 0-1 cable costs — Fixed Degree / Make It Connected / 0-1 MST. Score = f(component sizes over time): dangers / pair counts as chemicals mix or edges activate — DZY / Edgy Trees / Kruskal contribution (ABC214D).

phases.goal: Spot that merges, not a plain template DSU/MST, are the mutable state: constraint edges, offline size contributions, dual forests, complement graphs, or range-closures.

must_hit.point: Recognize contest DSU when edges encode constraints (equality, relative distance, same color, allowed swaps) rather than plain undirected connectivity.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names at least one constraint family and says merges track those relations, not only components.

must_hit.point: Recognize Kruskal-offline contribution when the answer is a function of component sizes as edges are added light→heavy (or reverse), especially size_A·size_B on merges.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Says sort edges and accumulate a size-product contribution instead of querying paths live.

must_hit.point: Recognize dual forests, complement/0-1 MST, or range-union closure when ordinary single-forest Kruskal is not enough.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions two DSUs that must both accept an edge, unused-vertex set for the 0-graph, or forcing [min_id,max_id] connected.

must_hit.point: Recognize the ask when merges are the only mutable state or a threshold edge weight defines connectivity among specials.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Ties the prompt to merge-only bookkeeping or Kruskal until k specials share a component.

probes: What in the statement says this is constraint DSU, Kruskal size-contribution, dual forests, complement MST, or range closure rather than template find/union?
When would you process edges offline by weight instead of answering each path query with LCA?

hints.1: Look past ‘run DSU’ — ask what the edges mean and what the score tracks as components change.
hints.2: Constraint relations, size products on merges, two forests, dense 0-edges, or interval closure are the depth signals.
hints.3: Say: equality/distance/color/swap edges → constraint DSU; answer = f(sizes) light→heavy → Kruskal contribution; dual/complement/range → specialized forest models.

phases.goal: Pick the right depth model: potential DSU, Kruskal contribution, equal-weight batching, complement components, range closure, dual forests, virtual star, or fixed-degree ST.

must_hit.point: Weighted/potential DSU: store delta[v]=value(v)−value(parent); on find compress deltas; union(a,b,w) sets val[b]−val[a]=w and reject inconsistent relates.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes potential on parent links, path-compressed deltas, and inconsistency detection (People on a Line / Third Letter).

must_hit.point: Kruskal contribution: sort edges ascending; merging A,B of weight w adds w·|A|·|B| toward sum of max-edge on path (ABC214D / Child and Zoo / Path Queries skeleton).
must_hit.evidence_hint: States the w·|A|·|B| merge contribution after sorting light→heavy.

must_hit.point: Same-weight batching: before unioning weight-w edges, count how many could still link different components; extras that fail after the batch force +1 ops to uniquify MST.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes count-then-union per equal-weight batch (MST Unification).

must_hit.point: 0-1 MST: MST weight = (#components in the 0-edge graph)−1; build those components via a set of unused vertices — never enumerate K_n.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Gives comps−1 and set-iteration over the complement of sparse 1-edges.

must_hit.point: Virtual star MST: connect every vertex to the global-min a_i with weight a_i+a_u, then Kruskal on given edges ∪ star (Make It Connected).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Adds star edges from argmin a_i before sorting/Kruskal.

must_hit.point: Fixed-degree spanning tree: force exactly k edges incident to vertex 1 — DSU-partition the rest, then pick which 1-edges close components.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Removes 1, components the remainder, then chooses exactly k bridges from 1.

probes: Walk through potential DSU relate(a,b,w) and when you reject.
For sum of max-edge on path, what do you add on each Kruskal merge?

hints.1: Match the ask to one of the eight depth tricks, not generic Kruskal.
hints.2: Potentials for differences; size products for path-max sums; batch equal weights; set for 0-1; star for cheap hub; k bridges from 1 for fixed degree.
hints.3: Relate via compressed deltas; on merge add w·|A|·|B|; batch same w before union; 0-1 cost = comps−1 via unused-vertex set; Kruskal given∪star; deg(1)=k via DSU then k bridges.

phases.goal: Encode potential-UFF, merge formulas, next-pointer range unions, complement set walks, dual-union gates, and letter/string node maps correctly.

must_hit.point: Potential/weighted DSU API: find returns root and compresses delta; expose relate(a,b,w) / same / inconsistency detect.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Sketches find that rewrites deltas along the path and a relate that checks existing relative values.

must_hit.point: On merge of sizes A,B know cold: components−1, A·B (= binom(A+B,2)−binom(A,2)−binom(B,2)), and weight contribution w·A·B.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States those three merge formulas without deriving them on the spot.

must_hit.point: Range unions: maintain next[i] = first index not yet united with i (or DSU on next pointer) so [l,r] is O((r-l)α^{-1}) amortized total.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes jumping via next[] while unioning the interval (Restructuring Company / Harmonious-style).

must_hit.point: Complement / 0-1 MST: iterate neighbors of the sparse missing edges and erase from a global set — never build K_n.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Keeps a set of unused vertices and erases reached ones during BFS/DSU.

must_hit.point: Letter/string DSU: map char→node or position→node; majority vote per component or spanning forest on 26 letters.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Cites Socks/K-Complete majority or Love Rescue forest on 26 nodes.

probes: How does find update deltas, and what are the three size-merge formulas you need cold?
How do you union a whole [l,r] without quadratic naive unions?

hints.1: API and bookkeeping matter as much as the high-level trick.
hints.2: Compress deltas on find; keep size formulas; use next[] for ranges; set-erase for complement; 26-letter or position nodes for strings.
hints.3: find rewrites delta[v]; formulas: comps−1, A·B, w·A·B; next[i] jumps unmerged indices; complement walks a set; letters use 26 nodes or position majority.

phases.goal: Justify amortized range unions, avoiding K_n materialization, and Kruskal on given edges plus a linear star.

must_hit.point: Range unions with next-pointer DSU make [l,r] O((r-l)α^{-1}) amortized total, not quadratic naive pairwise unions.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States the amortized bound and that each index is jumped past once.

must_hit.point: Complement / 0-1 MST must not enumerate K_n; set-iteration over unused vertices keeps work tied to the sparse 1-edges plus vertex erasures.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Refuses O(n^2) clique build and names set BFS/DSU instead.

must_hit.point: Virtual-star Make It Connected runs Kruskal on m+n edges (given edges ∪ star), not a rebuilt dense graph.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Counts m+n candidate edges after attaching the star.

probes: Why is range union with a next pointer amortized near-linear in the interval length?
Why can’t you build the complete 0-edge graph for 0-1 MST?

hints.1: Complexity fails come from naive intervals or dense complements.
hints.2: next[] jumps; unused-vertex set replaces K_n; star adds only n edges.
hints.3: Cite O((r-l)α^{-1}) for [l,r]; comps via set not K_n; Kruskal on m+n after the star.

phases.goal: Catch depth-pass failure modes: LCA-per-pair, built K_n, uncompressed potentials, unbatched equal weights, and naive range unions.

must_hit.point: When the statement says max edge on path ≤ x or sum of max edges, sort edges and DSU offline — do not LCA every pair.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Rejects all-pairs LCA and commits to offline Kruskal/DSU.

must_hit.point: For 0-1 MST / complement connectivity, never build K_n; use a set of unused vertices and the sparse missing-edge adjacency.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Flags clique construction as wrong and names set-iteration.

must_hit.point: Weighted DSU that forgets to compress deltas on find (or skips inconsistency checks) silently accepts bad difference constraints.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Requires path-compressed deltas and reject-on-conflict in relate.

must_hit.point: MST Unification: unioning same-weight edges one-by-one without a pre-batch count misses edges that could replace a tree edge (+1 ops).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Counts cross-component candidates before applying the weight-w batch.

must_hit.point: Range [l,r] unions without a next-unmerged pointer degrade; Harmonious-style closure still must force each component to swallow [min_id,max_id].
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions next-DSU and post-merge interval closure.

probes: What’s wrong with answering sum-of-max-edge queries with LCA on every pair?
Where do candidates lose ops on unique-MST or blow up on 0-1 MST?

hints.1: Depth bugs are modeling shortcuts that ignore the checklist.
hints.2: Offline Kruskal vs LCA; set vs K_n; compress deltas; batch equal weights; next[] + range closure.
hints.3: Sort+DSU for path-max sums; set for 0-1; find compresses delta; count then union per w; next-pointer [l,r] and force [min,max].

tradeoffs.topic: Weighted/potential DSU vs plain equality DSU
tradeoffs.strong_answer: When constraints are relative distances (val[b]−val[a]=w), store and compress deltas on find and reject inconsistent relates; plain same-component DSU only handles equality/partition.

tradeoffs.topic: Offline Kruskal size contribution vs LCA every pair
tradeoffs.strong_answer: For sum of max-edge on path (or max edge ≤ x offline), sort edges and add w·|A|·|B| on merges; do not LCA every pair.

tradeoffs.topic: Virtual star ∪ given edges vs rebuilding a dense hub graph
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Connect every vertex to global-min a_i with weight a_i+a_u and Kruskal on given edges ∪ star (m+n edges) — Make It Connected — instead of materializing all pairwise hub options.
0-1 MST cost is (#components in the 0-edge graph)−1; iterate a set of unused vertices against sparse 1-edges — never enumerate K_n.
When an edge is legal only if both forests would accept it (Graph Composition / Mocha-style), maintain two DSUs and count merges needed to equalize after removing contradictions.

tradeoffs.topic: Equal-weight batching vs immediate per-edge union
tradeoffs.strong_answer: To uniquify an MST, before unioning weight-w edges count how many could still link different components; extras that fail after the batch cost +1 (MST Unification).

gotchas.trap: Answering “max edge on path ≤ x” / “sum of max edges” with LCA on every pair.
gotchas.correction: Sort edges and run DSU offline (Kruskal contribution / threshold connectivity).
MST weight = comps−1 in the 0-edge graph; iterate a set of unused vertices against sparse missing edges.

gotchas.trap: Potential DSU without compressing deltas on find, or without inconsistency checks.
gotchas.correction: find returns root and rewrites deltas; relate(a,b,w) rejects when the implied difference conflicts.

gotchas.trap: Unioning equal-weight edges immediately when the goal is a unique MST.
gotchas.correction: Per equal-weight batch, count cross-component candidates first; extras that fail after the batch need +1 ops.

gotchas.trap: Naive pairwise unions on [l,r] or forgetting Harmonious range closure.
gotchas.correction: Maintain next[i] (first index not united with i) for amortized O((r-l)α^{-1}); after ordinary merges force each component to swallow [min_id,max_id].

gotchas.trap: Forgetting the three merge size formulas under contribution / clique / component-count asks.
gotchas.correction: Know cold: components−1, A·B (= binom(A+B,2)−binom(A,2)−binom(B,2)), and w·A·B.

gotchas.trap: Dual-forest problems treated as one DSU.
gotchas.correction: Add an edge only if both unions succeed; count remaining merges to match components after removing contradictions.
